method: Lighthouse 13.4 lab runs (27 runs: Tier-1 URLs 3× mobile + 1× desktop, Tier-2 1×+1×) + live Playwright probes + curl header matrix + fresh vite build + static source analysis. Every finding carries directly reproduced evidence.

findings.title: Mobile LCP fails the 2.5 s Core Web Vitals threshold on every key public route
findings.evidence: lighthouse/summary.json — mobile LCP medians: home 5.28 s (runs 4.78/5.28/5.33), demo-invite 5.95 s (4.39/5.95/6.23), templates 5.13 s (5.12/5.13/5.29), confirm 3.6 s, login 4.2 s, terms 4.2 s; mobile perf scores 63–83. LCP breakdown (home.mobile.report.json lcp-breakdown-insight): TTFB 489 ms + element render delay 2,480 ms — the LCP element is text render-blocked by font CSS + JS boot, not a slow image.
findings.metric_impact: Mobile perf 63–83; LCP 3.6–6.2 s vs ≤2.5 s target; desktop passes everywhere (82–98)
findings.fix_recommendation: Attack render delay: fix the font pipeline (PERF-02), trim the 654 KB main chunk (PERF-05), and inline/prioritize the hero text styles. The audience is WhatsApp-mobile-first, so mobile LCP is the single most user-visible web-quality metric this platform has.
findings.cross_ref: New ground — the 2026-06-20 audit deliberately skipped numeric CWV measurement

findings.title: Render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet: 5 families × 19 weights costs ~900 ms before first render
findings.evidence: frontend/index.html:23 (one blocking css2 request for Cairo/Amiri/Noto Naskh/Heebo/Frank Ruhl Libre, display=swap); home.mobile.report.json render-blocking-insight: 888 ms wasted on that stylesheet; live probes: 10 woff2 files fetched on landing, 17 on the invite page.
findings.metric_impact: 888 ms render-blocking on mobile home; primary driver of the 2.4 s LCP render delay; also the root cause of PERF-04 desktop CLS
findings.fix_recommendation: Subset to the 2–3 families actually critical per language, self-host woff2 with <link rel=preload> for the hero-critical faces, prefer variable fonts (one file per family instead of 5 weights), and add size-adjusted local fallbacks (font-display: swap is already set). Per .agents/skills/performance/SKILL.md §Font optimization.

findings.title: 7.7 MB of orphaned face-api model shards are deployed on every release (64% of dist)
findings.evidence: frontend/public/models/ = 7.7 MB of 12 MB dist (build-stats.md); zero references in frontend/src or backend (grep); live network probes confirm /models/* never fetched on any public route; headers.md: served publicly with cache-control no-cache.
findings.metric_impact: No runtime cost to users (never fetched), but 7.7 MB deployed dead weight per release, publicly downloadable, and pure hosting/deploy waste
findings.fix_recommendation: Delete frontend/public/models/ (face matching moved server-side to AWS Rekognition; backend faceIndex/match.ts only consumes descriptors). Verify the Expo app doesn't reference the hosted URLs before removal.

findings.title: Desktop CLS failure caused by late web-font swap re-flowing the whole page
findings.evidence: confirm.desktop.report.json: CLS 0.324 (fail, >0.25); cls-culprits-insight attributes 0.322 to the <html> element with the Amiri woff2 from fonts.gstatic as sub-item cause. help.desktop CLS 0.217 (needs improvement). Mobile CLS ≈0 on the same pages (summary.json).
findings.metric_impact: CLS 0.324 / 0.217 desktop vs ≤0.1 target; the public RSVP form visibly jumps while a guest is starting to fill it
findings.fix_recommendation: Preload the 1–2 critical Arabic/Hebrew faces and define size-adjust/ascent-override fallback metrics so the swap doesn't change line heights (bundled with the PERF-02 font rework).

findings.title: 654 KB main entry chunk with no vendor-splitting strategy
findings.evidence: build-stats.md: index-mHFYgxkl.js 654.55 KB (215.61 KB gzip); Vite emitted its own >500 KB warning; frontend/vite.config.js has no build block (no manualChunks). Route-level React.lazy splitting is otherwise good (portals, analytics, liveness, three.js all split).
findings.metric_impact: ~216 KB gzip parsed+executed before any route renders; contributes to the 2.4 s LCP render delay on mobile
findings.fix_recommendation: Add build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks to split react/react-dom/router vendor from app code, and audit the entry for portal-only utilities that can move behind the lazy boundaries.
findings.cross_ref: wiki/Tasks-Backlog.md TASK-009 (bundle size) — partially addressed by per-role splits; entry chunk remains

findings.title: 6 s Cloud Function cold start on the guest invite shell (/d/**)
findings.evidence: headers.md: first GET /d/demo/demo?demo=1 TTFB 5.99 s, immediate second request 0.39 s — the digitalInvitePreview rewrite (firebase.json) eats a full cold start before the 3.3 KB shell is served.
findings.metric_impact: First guest to open an invite after an idle period waits ~6 s on a blank screen before the SPA even starts loading; invisible in warm lab runs (demo-invite LCP 5.95 s is on TOP of a warm shell)
findings.fix_recommendation: Set minInstances: 1 on digitalInvitePreview (small monthly cost, kills the worst guest first impression), or serve the shell statically and inject OG tags at the CDN/edge layer.
findings.cross_ref: The product's own field metrics (inviteMetrics.js → POST /invites/digital/metrics) can quantify how many real guests hit cold starts

findings.title: Non-hashed static assets are never cached (favicon, OG image, manifest)
findings.evidence: headers.md: all three served cache-control: no-cache (they fall under the ** rule; only /assets/** gets immutable). og-default.png is 110 KB and is re-fetched by every share-preview crawl.
findings.metric_impact: Repeat fetches of ~125 KB of stable brand assets on every visit/crawl
findings.fix_recommendation: Add firebase.json header rules giving these paths public, max-age=86400 (or version them into /assets/).

findings.title: No responsive/modern image delivery (srcset, WebP/AVIF) and most static imgs lack lazy loading
findings.evidence: build-stats.md greps: srcset usage 0; 14 of 17 tags without loading attribute (the digital-invite gallery DOES use loading=lazy + alt="", console-network.md). Only 17 raster imgs exist app-wide (brand art is inline SVG/canvas) so impact is bounded.
findings.metric_impact: Bounded — few raster images; og-default.png 110 KB is the largest
findings.fix_recommendation: Add loading="lazy" to below-fold imgs and serve WebP where a raster is used; low priority given the SVG-first architecture.

findings.title: Color-contrast failures on muted gold text (terms/help footers and the invite venue block)
findings.evidence: terms.mobile + help.mobile color-contrast audit: #7a6a4a on #07070a = 3.82:1 at 12 px (needs 4.5:1). demo-invite.mobile: venue rows #a07840 on #f8f6f0 = 3.69:1 and venue label #ad8b5a on #f8f6f0 = 2.93:1 at bold 10 px. Lighthouse a11y scores: terms 89, help 92, demo-invite 96.
findings.metric_impact: WCAG 2.1 AA 1.4.3 failures on the guest-facing invitation (venue details) and legal pages
findings.fix_recommendation: Bump the muted-gold tokens: #7a6a4a → ~#95835f on the dark theme, and darken the venue-info golds on the light invite background to ≥4.5:1 (e.g. #8a6530). These are theme-token changes, so the fix is a few lines.
findings.cross_ref: Existing axe CI gate only fails on critical/serious — contrast is 'serious' in axe but these pages/elements aren't in the gated set

findings.title: Heading-order violation on /terms (h3 follows without an h2 level)
findings.evidence: terms.mobile.report.json heading-order audit: <h3 style="font-family: Amiri..."> flagged as skipping a level.
findings.metric_impact: Screen-reader document outline is misleading on the legal page
findings.fix_recommendation: Change the section headings on TermsPage to the correct level (h2) or adjust the hierarchy.

findings.title: Small touch targets: consent checkbox 17×17 px (below WCAG 2.2 minimum); many controls under the 44 px comfort size
findings.evidence: Live DOM measurements (console-network.md): consent checkbox 17×17 (WCAG 2.5.8 minimum is 24×24 unless exempt); guest-count steppers 38×38; language toggle 38×28 / 39×33; landing has 23 interactive elements <44 px (nav CTA 81×36, footer contacts 36×36).
findings.metric_impact: Older guests on phones (a stated persona) mis-tap; the checkbox is the only element below the hard WCAG 2.2 line
findings.fix_recommendation: Give the checkbox a ≥24 px hit area (padding on the wrapping label), and lift steppers/language toggle to ≥44 px per the 44 px comfort rule in .agents/skills/accessibility/SKILL.md.
findings.cross_ref: wiki/Tasks-Backlog.md TASK-UX-4 (≥44 px touch targets) — STILL OPEN

findings.title: ~25 of 40 <label> elements in source are not htmlFor-associated (portal-internal forms)
findings.evidence: build-stats.md grep: 40 <label> vs 15 htmlFor in frontend/src. The public RSVP form is fully associated (live probe — all inputs htmlFor + 16 px), so the residue is in portal forms, which are only covered by the report-only authed axe spec.
findings.metric_impact: Screen-reader users in the groom/admin/driver portals may hear unlabeled inputs
findings.fix_recommendation: Sweep portal form fields with htmlFor/id pairs (or wrap inputs inside their labels); consider promoting the authed axe spec from report-only to gating on serious once clean.
findings.cross_ref: docs/WEB-AUDIT-2026-06-20.md Appendix B §5 — public-form half is FIXED, portal half remains

findings.title: No per-route or per-language head management — every page ships the identical Arabic title/description
findings.evidence: No head manager / document.title usage in frontend/src (grep); live probe: after switching to Hebrew, <html lang> updates but document.title stays Arabic; /templates, /terms, /help, /confirm all share the landing title (summary.json finalDisplayedUrl vs title).
findings.metric_impact: Browser tabs, bookmarks, history and non-/d/ share previews are indistinguishable; Hebrew-speaking users see an Arabic title everywhere (the product's own research frames language dignity as trust)
findings.fix_recommendation: A 15-line useDocumentTitle(route, lang) hook — no helmet dependency needed. Server-side OG injection already handles /d/** and /invite/** correctly.
findings.cross_ref: Organic SEO is deliberately deprioritized (robots.txt comments) — rated for UX/share value, not ranking

findings.title: Tokenized invite pages are indexable: the X-Robots-Tag noindex documented as a TODO in robots.txt was never implemented
findings.evidence: frontend/public/robots.txt comment: 'To explicitly de-index a tokenized response, add an X-Robots-Tag: noindex header in digitalInvitePreview.' Live check (headers.md): GET /d/demo/demo?demo=1 returns no X-Robots-Tag header.
findings.metric_impact: If any tokenized link is ever posted publicly (a guest shares it on Facebook), a page carrying couple names + wedding details becomes indexable — privacy-adjacent, not just SEO hygiene
findings.fix_recommendation: Add X-Robots-Tag: noindex to digitalInvitePreview responses (one line in the function). Keep robots.txt Allow so WhatsApp preview crawlers still work — noindex and preview-fetch are independent.

findings.title: Duplicate origin without canonical: dawa-aa793.web.app serves the full app
findings.evidence: headers.md: web.app origin returns the identical app; no <link rel=canonical> anywhere in the codebase (grep).
findings.metric_impact: Split identity for any links that circulate with the web.app URL; trivial ranking impact given the referral-first model
findings.fix_recommendation: Add <link rel="canonical" href="https://dawa.to<path>"> via the same head hook as SEO-01 (or at minimum a static canonical on the landing shell).

findings.title: www.dawa.to does not resolve (no DNS record)
findings.evidence: headers.md: dig returns nothing for www.dawa.to A/CNAME; curl connection fails. http→https on the apex 301s correctly.
findings.metric_impact: Anyone typing www. gets a browser error page instead of the site
findings.fix_recommendation: Add www CNAME → dawa.to (or Firebase Hosting custom-domain redirect) in DNS.
findings.cross_ref: CORS ALLOWED_ORIGINS already lists www.dawa.to, so the intent existed

findings.title: Soft-404s: unknown paths return 200 with the SPA shell (including /sitemap.xml)
findings.evidence: headers.md: GET /this-route-does-not-exist-xyz → 200 text/html (shell, same ETag as /); /sitemap.xml → 200 HTML. The router client-side redirects unknown routes to /.
findings.metric_impact: Crawlers index error paths as duplicates of the landing page; monitoring can't distinguish broken links from real pages
findings.fix_recommendation: Keep the SPA fallback, but render a real not-found view (with meta robots noindex) instead of silently redirecting to /. A sitemap is NOT recommended — deliberately skipped per the WhatsApp-first strategy.
findings.cross_ref: docs/WEB-AUDIT-2026-06-20.md rated organic SEO later/skip — consistent

findings.title: Missing /assets/* files are served as index.html with a 1-year immutable cache header — post-deploy cache poisoning
findings.evidence: headers.md: GET /assets/<nonexistent>.js → 200, content-type text/html, body = index.html (same ETag as /), cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable. Mechanism: firebase.json rewrites ** → /index.html AND applies the /assets/** immutable header rule to the rewritten response.
findings.metric_impact: After every deploy, any open tab that lazy-loads an old hashed chunk receives HTML-as-JS (module MIME error → broken navigation) and the browser caches that wrong response as immutable for a year for that URL. This is the classic 'app broken until hard refresh' failure, made persistent by the header.
findings.fix_recommendation: Two independent layers: (1) handle Vite's vite:preloadError event in frontend/src/main.jsx with a one-time location.reload() so stale-chunk tabs self-heal; (2) stop the poisoning: rewrite /assets/** to a tiny 404-returning function (or drop the immutable header for non-existent files by scoping the header rule to real hashed patterns and validating at deploy). Layer 1 alone removes the user-facing breakage.
findings.cross_ref: New ground — not in the 2026-06-20 audit

findings.title: npm audit: 1 critical (fast-xml-parser, 7 advisories) + 17 moderate vulnerabilities in production dependencies
findings.evidence: npm audit --omit=dev (2026-07-16): fast-xml-parser critical (DoS/entity-expansion/injection advisories incl. an incomplete-fix CVE-2026-26278 follow-up), pulled in via the @aws-sdk/AWS Amplify liveness chain; 17 moderate all in @aws-sdk/* packages. fixAvailable=true for the critical.
findings.metric_impact: Client-side DoS-class exposure (browser context limits exploitability — no server-side XML parsing of untrusted input was found), plus supply-chain hygiene debt; the security.yml dependency-review only gates NEW dependencies on PRs
findings.fix_recommendation: npm audit fix --prefix frontend (fix available), then bump the aws-amplify family (already an owner action from the 2026-07-02 security audit). Add a scheduled npm audit job to security.yml so drift is caught.
findings.cross_ref: wiki Security Audit 2026-07-02 open item 'bump aws-amplify' — STILL OPEN

findings.title: PWA is declared but not installable: no service worker, SVG-only icon
findings.evidence: site.webmanifest declares display: standalone with a single SVG icon (sizes: any); live probe: navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() → 0; no sw.js in dist.
findings.metric_impact: Add-to-home-screen prompts never fire; installed-app experience promised by the manifest doesn't exist
findings.fix_recommendation: Either finish it (192/512 PNG icons + a minimal offline-shell service worker via vite-plugin-pwa) or remove display: standalone so the manifest stops over-promising. For a WhatsApp-link product, install-ability is genuinely optional — deciding explicitly is the point.

findings.title: Dormant Netlify deploy config carries none of the security/cache headers
findings.evidence: netlify.toml (repo root): build + SPA redirect only — no HSTS/CSP/nosniff/cache rules, while firebase.json defines all of them. No live Netlify URL found in the repo.
findings.metric_impact: If the Netlify target is ever revived, the same app ships with zero security headers and no immutable asset caching
findings.fix_recommendation: Delete netlify.toml if Netlify is dead, or mirror the firebase.json headers into it.

findings.title: CSP lacks frame-ancestors (modern clickjacking control); otherwise headers are exemplary
findings.evidence: headers.md: CSP has object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self' but no frame-ancestors directive; X-Frame-Options: DENY covers legacy browsers. HSTS preload 2y, nosniff, referrer-policy, permissions-policy all present; console 0 errors on all tested pages; Leaflet CDN is SRI-pinned.
findings.metric_impact: Minor: XFO DENY already blocks framing in practice; frame-ancestors is the standards-track successor
findings.fix_recommendation: Add frame-ancestors 'none' to the CSP in firebase.json (keep XFO for old browsers), per .agents/skills/best-practices/SKILL.md.

findings.title: FIXED since 2026-06-20: public-form label association (the prior audit's headline a11y finding)
findings.evidence: Live probe: every input on /confirm/groom is htmlFor-associated (text, tel, city, street, house number, checkbox). Prior audit reported zero htmlFor in all of frontend/src.
findings.fix_recommendation: None — recorded as fixed. Portal-side residue tracked as A11Y-04.

findings.title: FIXED since 2026-06-20: iOS input-zoom (16 px inputs)
findings.evidence: GlobalStyle.jsx:131-132 sets .input-field font-size: 16px with an explicit iOS comment; live probe: all RSVP inputs computed 16 px.
findings.fix_recommendation: None — fixed.

findings.title: ADDRESSED: reduced-motion fallbacks now cover landing + invite + splash (TASK-UX-7 motion half)
findings.evidence: prefers-reduced-motion respected in 8 files: LandingPage.jsx, GlobalStyle.jsx, index.html splash, InviteStyles.jsx, CelestialAmbience.jsx, introContract.js, destination-love/Styles.jsx, haptics.js/useDeviceCapability.js.
findings.fix_recommendation: None — verified present.

findings.title: STILL OPEN (benign): TASK-UX-1's hardcoded left:50% scroll cue survives, but it centers correctly in RTL
findings.evidence: InviteStyles.jsx:100 still uses left: 50% + translateX(-50%) for .dawa-inv-cue. Centering via left:50% is direction-neutral, so no visible RTL bug; the backlog's logical-properties cleanup remains cosmetic debt.
findings.fix_recommendation: Fold into the next TASK-UX-1 pass (inset-inline-start or keep — visual behavior is correct today).

findings.title: NEW capability since the prior audit: real-user Core Web Vitals field pipeline exists on invites
findings.evidence: frontend/src/utils/inviteMetrics.js lazily loads web-vitals and POSTs TTFB/LCP/CLS/INP (+sealed/ready/tap timings) to /invites/digital/metrics with keepalive/sendBeacon.
findings.metric_impact: The lab-only caveat of this report can be validated against real guests for the money page; also partially delivers TASK-UX-6's funnel instrumentation
findings.fix_recommendation: Surface these field vitals in the admin analytics page and use them to verify the PERF-01/02 fixes on real guests.

findings.title: STILL OPEN: no performance job in CI (prior audit said skip; today's numbers justify a lightweight budget)
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml has unit/build/integration/e2e/prod-smoke/gitleaks but no Lighthouse or bundle-size budget; the 2026-06-20 audit explicitly rated Lighthouse-CI as over-engineering. Today's measured mobile LCP failures change that calculus.
findings.fix_recommendation: Minimal version: a nightly npx lighthouse run on / and the demo invite with a JSON assert on perf score ≥ 80 mobile, using this report's Reports/lighthouse/ output as the baseline.
